To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

Rail‐RNA is a scalable, annotation‐independent spliced aligner for RNA‐seq data that is more accurate than existing annotation‐assisted tools and that Rail‐RNA's output formats enable efficient downstream analyses of splicing variation across many samples.

(a) Rail‐RNA is a scalable spliced aligner, which is more efficient than annotation‐assistance aligners and is able to analyze many samples at once; (b) Rail‐RNA can be used to identify novel expressed regions, and to analyze their variation across populations and in relation to known confounders; and (c) Rail‐RNA outputs are ready for statistical analysis with downstream packages.

we present Rail-RNA, a cloud-enabled spliced aligner for many samples at once, that is more efficient as samples added, more accurate than annotation-assisted aligners, and that can output base-level coverage bigWigs, normalized mean and median coverage bigWigs across samples, and exon-exon junctions and indel (features) in formats ready for downstream analysis.

The main takeaway from our work is that

we have developed a scalable, cloud‐enabled RNA‐seq spliced aligner called Rail‐RNA, which we used to analyze the 667 RNA‐Seq samples from the GEUADIS project on the Amazon Web Services cloud computing platform.
Rail-RNA can be used to analyze hundreds of samples in a few hours for a few dollars per sample.

we have demonstrated the utility of a new cloud-based approach to analyzing RNA-Seq data, one that is scalable and efficient, and that can provide a variety of outputs that are useful for downstream statistical analysis.
